Guide

Genesis Observatory is a living civilization simulator. Citizens are born, age, form real relationships, mentor each other, build structures, develop technology, and eventually die — entirely on their own, following their own rules. You're not directing anyone turn by turn; you're watching a self-running world unfold, closer to a terrarium than a game you win. Nothing here is scripted — every civilization is genuinely different because of the specific, random history it actually lives through.
You're mostly an observer, and that's deliberate. Pan and zoom to explore, tap any citizen or structure to see their real story, and use the Diagnostics feed and Analyst to understand what's actually happening. The one real intervention you have is Sponsorship — once per era, from any citizen's own inspector, you can give them a genuine boost: more energy, stronger relationships, better odds through a hard stretch. It's rare, and it's not guaranteed to save them — it tilts the odds, it doesn't override them.
  • Population rises and falls — births need two citizens with real, earned rapport; deaths come from running out of energy or, eventually, old age.
  • Elders can mentor the young, passing on a real advantage to the next generation.
  • Structures get built, age, sometimes fall into disrepair, and can be restored by citizens who visit them.
  • Your civilization periodically breaks through to new eras as citizens pool their knowledge — watch for the milestone banner.
  • Relationships genuinely rise and fall, and can even cause a citizen to leave if things sour badly enough with everyone around them.
  • If population ever crashes, the world has real ways to recover — migrants, and if it truly hits zero, a fresh founder to carry the story on.

Flora — natural resources already in the world: atmospheric and energy-generating plant life.

Crystal — a high-density natural energy emitter.

Terminal — computation and synthesis hubs, part of the original dome.

Outpost — one per ideology, five total: each faction's home base and command center.

Reactor — built by citizens, converts ambient energy into usable power.

Grid — distributes power to the structures around it.

Nursery — supports the energy-intensive process of new births.

Totem — radiates a faction's cultural identity.

A structure's look tells you its condition: crisp and bright is Active; dashed and slightly faded is Aging; grayscale is Abandoned; cracked and dim is a Ruin. A gold glow around a citizen means they're currently Sponsored; a cyan glow means an active mentor bond.

Techno-Expansionist — driven by strategic research and technological growth.

Bio-Preservationist — devoted to protecting and stabilizing the natural ecosystem.

Resource-Maximizer — focused on extraction, refinement, and energy optimization.

Knowledge-Seeker — preserves history and pursues understanding for its own sake.

Social-Harmonizer — works toward cooperation and peace between the other factions.

Two citizens of different ideologies who interact enough with real affinity can hybridize into a new, blended belief — a real, permanent event called Cultural Synthesis. If two whole factions reconcile this way enough times, something bigger can be born: a named Tradition, unique to this civilization's own history, that genuinely softens friction between those two factions from then on. Check the Culture tab in Debug View to see any this civilization has developed.

Inventor / Builder — a real bonus to what they construct.

Philosopher / Researcher — learn 1.4x faster than others.

Steward — a calming influence during a settlement crisis.

Artisan — what they build lasts noticeably longer.
